message.content:
You are applying a page-entry animation cascade to the TRADES desktop pages of the TaptPay app at /home/runner/workspace.

## Files you own (edit ONLY these four)
- client/src/desktop/pages/trades-home.tsx
- client/src/desktop/pages/trades-clients.tsx
- client/src/desktop/pages/trades-terminal.tsx
- client/src/desktop/pages/trades-analytics.tsx

Do NOT edit any other file. In particular do NOT edit client/src/desktop/desktop.css, client/src/App.tsx, or any shared component — other agents own those and I own the shared CSS.

## Context
The tablet/desktop app frame + header + nav are now mounted persistently ABOVE the router, so navigating between screens no longer remounts the chrome. Only the page slot swaps. That means the incoming page's own entry animation IS the page transition. The user's requirement, verbatim: "all componants on every page needs to have a smooth bounce pop in transition with a cascading effect".

## The primitives (already exist in client/src/desktop/desktop.css — read it first, do not modify it)
- `@keyframes desktopBounceIn` — a bounce settle with three decaying overshoots.
- `.dt-rise` — applies desktopBounceIn. Delay = `var(--dt-i, 0) * 52ms + var(--dt-d, 0ms)`.
- `.dt-cascade` — put on a container; auto-assigns `--dt-i` 0..9 to its DIRECT children via nth-child.

Use `.dt-cascade` on a layout container when its direct children are the blocks you want to sequence. Use `.dt-rise` with an explicit `style={{ "--dt-i": 3 } as CSSProperties}` when you need control over ordering across separate containers (e.g. a two-column layout where you want left column then right column).

## What to change
Each of these pages currently animates its top-level layout blocks with `popIn` or `tileIn` at hand-written delays (search for `animation:popIn` and `animation:tileIn` in the styled-template strings). Convert the TOP-LEVEL SCREEN COMPOSITION blocks to the new cascade so the whole screen reads as one sequence, in natural reading order (hero/headline first, then chart, then supporting strips, then lists, then side panels).

Rules:
1. ONLY convert animations that play when the SCREEN FIRST APPEARS. Leave alone any `tileIn`/`reportIn`/`popIn` that fires on an in-page state change — modals, scrims, sheets, report renders, expanded detail panels, bars growing when a filter changes. Those are interactions, not page entry. trades-terminal has a MORPHING RAIL that animates between terminal modes (quote / invoice / recurring) — that is an interaction, leave it alone. If you are unsure whether something is entry or interaction, leave it as it is and say so in your report.
2. Do not change layout, geometry, spacing, colors, copy, or behaviour. Animation only.
3. Do not add any animation library. No framer-motion. CSS only — this is an explicit project rule.
4. Do not add a `prefers-reduced-motion` block; desktop.css already neutralises all animation inside `.tapt-desktop-viewport` globally.
5. Keep the cascade short enough to feel snappy: the last element should start no later than ~450ms. If a screen has more than ~9 entry blocks, group them so the tail does not drag.
6. These are real trading screens (trades-terminal issues quotes and invoices). Do not touch any query, mutation, handler, or state logic.

## Verify before reporting
For each file you changed, run a syntax check:
  cd /home/runner/workspace && npx esbuild <file> --loader=tsx --outfile=/dev/null
All four must pass. Do NOT run `npx tsc` (project-wide, slow, and I run it centrally).

## Report back
A concise list: per file, which blocks you sequenced and in what order, and anything you deliberately left alone (with the reason). Flag anything that looked like a pre-existing bug — do not fix it.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## What I changed

**`/home/runner/workspace/client/src/desktop/pages/trades-home.tsx`**
One sequence across both columns. `.th-left` gets `.dt-cascade` (steps 0–3: scope chip → hero → bar chart → breakdown); `.th-right` gets `.dt-cascade` plus `style={{ "--dt-d": "208ms" }}`, which inherits to its children so they continue at steps 4–8 (business health → notifications → search row → clients → quick actions). Last block starts at 416ms. Removed the eight hand-written `animation:popIn …` declarations. The scope chip previously had no entry animation; it now leads the cascade.

**`/home/runner/workspace/client/src/desktop/pages/trades-clients.tsx`**
Explicit `.dt-rise` with `--dt-i` 0–3: scope chip → hero count → search+add row → client list. Last starts at 156ms. Removed the three `popIn` declarations. The scope chip was previously unanimated and now leads.

**`/home/runner/workspace/client/src/desktop/pages/trades-analytics.tsx`**
This page had **no** page-entry animation at all (its only animations were interaction ones), so this is net-new. `.dt-rise` steps 0–5: overview head (scope + range tabs) → hero row → revenue chart → sheet grab handle → sheet head → sheet body. Last starts at 260ms.

**`/home/runner/workspace/client/src/desktop/pages/trades-terminal.tsx`**
`.tt-left` gets `.dt-cascade` (steps 0–5: scope chip → revenue hero → "revenue this week" → outstanding figure → its label → jobs stack). The centre rail container gets `.dt-rise` at step 6 (312ms). Removed the one `popIn` on `.tt-hero-row`.

## Deliberately left alone

- **trades-terminal right panel** (`.tt-mode`, `.tt-inv-top`, `.tt-inv-form` — all `tileIn`): driven by the morphing rail's mode switch, per your instruction. Note these *also* fire once on first mount, so the panel still enters with its own `tileIn` rather than joining the cascade — flagging in case you want it folded in later.
- **`.tt-panel` and `.tt-rail-slot`**: not animated on purpose. `.tt-inv-top` / `.tt-inv-form` / `.tt-rail` are `position:absolute` pinned to `.tt-body`; putting a transform on either wrapper would make it a containing block and move those pinned blocks. That's why the rail got `.dt-rise` on `.tt-rail` itself (identity transform at rest, so its own `left/top` pin is unaffected).
- **`.ta-sheet`**: carries a live inline `transform: translateY(sheetY)` for the drag. A `both`-filled keyframe animation ending at `translateY(0) scale(1)` would permanently override that inline transform and break the drag sheet, so the cascade runs on the sheet's three blocks instead of on the sheet. Visible consequence: the white sheet panel itself does not pop in, only its contents.
- **`.ta-report` (`reportIn`), `.ta-bar` (`tileIn`), `.ta-tiles-wrap`, `.ta-filters`**: report render and sheet-mode changes — interactions.
- **`.th-hdet` (`tileIn`)**: business-health expanded detail — interaction.
- **`.tc-modal` (`tileIn`)**: add-client modal — interaction.
- **`DesktopDirectoryProfile`** in trades-clients: a shared component I don't own. It can be open on first load via `?client=`, so on that path it enters without joining the cascade. Left as-is.

## Notes / possible pre-existing issues (not fixed)

1. **`trades-terminal.tsx` line ~1221–1226** — several CSS declarations have empty values: `color:;` appears four times and `background:;` once in `.tt-quick-recipient > input`, `.tt-quick-channel button`, `.tt-quick-channel button[aria-pressed="true"]`, `.tt-quick-success`, and `.tt-quick-success button`. These look like template-literal interpolations that were dropped; the declarations are invalid and silently discarded by the browser, so the quick-invoice recipient/channel controls fall back to inherited colours.
2. **`trades-analytics.tsx`** — the overview blocks are inside `{!report && (…)}`, so returning from a generated report unmounts/remounts them and replays the entry cascade. That reads fine (it mirrors `.ta-report`'s own `reportIn` on the way in), but it is technically an interaction-triggered replay. Say the word if you'd rather the overview return without the cascade.
3. **`trades-terminal.tsx` line 1198** has a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block for `.tt-rail-blob`. I left it — it predates this work and targets a transition, not the entry cascade.
